summary_responses.response: The paper introduces DiffTry, a lightweight, distributed, and stateless retry mechanism that assigns class-specific retry limits to prioritize high-value microservice transactions during overloads without needing coordination, overload sensing, or application changes. Traditional retries ignore priority, fail to protect premium traffic, and can amplify load into retry storms, whereas DiffTry embeds differentiation directly into retry budgets so high-priority requests succeed more often while remaining silent under normal load. Analytical models using fluid approximations and queueing theory first capture per-stream throughput and rejections for a single overloaded service, then generalize to arbitrary networks via an extended open-network flow model whose equations are solved iteratively. The framework proves convergence, uniqueness for DAG topologies, network-wide monotonicity of success rates with retry limits, and substantial protection of high-priority traffic even under adversarial overloads. Simulations and a live Kubernetes service-mesh deployment confirm that measured end-to-end rejection rates closely match the analysis, establishing DiffTry as an effective drop-in prioritization tool.

key_fact_breakdown.key_fact: DiffTry (Differential Retries) is a stateless mechanism that assigns different retry-attempt limits to different priority classes of requests to achieve differentiation in rejection rates.

summary_responses.response: The Office of Personnel Management is issuing a direct final rule to make technical revisions to its Family and Medical Leave Act regulations that incorporate statutory amendments from 2021 and 2023. These changes expand FMLA eligibility by counting virtually all Federal civilian service (including temporary or intermittent) plus certain honorable active military service toward the 12-month qualifying service requirement. The rule also confirms that annual or sick leave earned under non-title 5 authorities may be substituted for unpaid FMLA leave and excludes certain Veterans Health Administration employees from title 5 FMLA coverage. Because paid parental leave is substituted for unpaid FMLA leave, the same eligibility updates apply to PPL as well. The rule takes effect December 14, 2026, unless significant adverse comments are received by November 16, 2026.
